record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Alternating paths in embedded segment visibility graphs
record.original_question: In the embedded segment visibility graph G′ of a set S of n disjoint segments, is there always an alternating path containing at least O(log n) segments of S?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 In the embedded segment visibility graph G′ of a set S of n disjoint segments, there exists an alternating path containing at least O(log n) segments of S.
Urratia [115] made the following conjecture which was proved by Hoffmann and Tóth [64].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \{s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n\}$ be a set of $n$ pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane (in general position, with no three endpoints collinear). The embedded segment visibility graph $G'$ of $S$ is defined as follows: its vertex set consists of the $2n$ endpoints of the segments in $S$; its edge set contains (i) every segment $s_i \in S$ (called a segment edge), and (ii) every visibility edge $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are endpoints of two distinct segments such that the open line segment between $p$ and $q$ does not intersect any segment of $S$. An alternating path in $G'$ is a simple path that alternates between segment edges and visibility edges.

Prove or disprove: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that for every set $S$ of $n$ pairwise disjoint segments in general position, the embedded segment visibility graph $G'$ contains an alternating path that uses at least $c \log n$ segment edges of $S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, originally posed by Urrutia, was proved by Hoffmann and Tóth, who showed that the embedded segment visibility graph of $n$ disjoint segments always contains an alternating path traversing at least $\Omega(\log n)$ segments.
